title: Problem Overview
content: Erdős Problem #374: For $m \in \mathbb{N}$, define $F(m)$ as the minimal $k \geq 2$ such that there exist integers $2 \leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots < a_k = m$ with $a_1! \cdot a_2! \cdots a_k!$ a perfect square. Then $D_k = \{m : F(m) = k\}$. It is known that $D_2$ is the set of perfect squares (minus singletons), $D_k$ is finite for $k \geq 3$, and $D_k = \emptyset$ for $k \geq 7$. The open question concerns the growth rate of $|D_k|$.
mathContext: $F(m) = \min\{k \geq 2 : \exists\, 2 \leq a_1 < \cdots < a_k = m,\; \prod a_i! \in \square\}$. Then $D_k = F^{-1}(k)$.

title: Factorial Product Definitions
content: Five core definitions: `IsPerfectSquare n` (exists $k$ with $n = k^2$), `factorialProduct seq` (product of factorials along a list), `HasSquareFactorialProduct m k` (existence of a valid sequence of length $k$ ending at $m$ whose factorial product is a perfect square), `bigF m` (the minimum such $k$, or 0 if none exists — a noncomputable `Nat.find`), and `inDk k m` (membership in $D_k$, i.e., $F(m) = k$).

title: Basic Properties
content: Two basic results: `bigF_ge_two` proves $F(m) \geq 2$ whenever $F(m)$ is defined, using `split_ifs` to handle the conditional definition. `factorialProduct_pair` computes the factorial product of a two-element list $[a,b]$ as $a! \cdot b!$.

title: D2 = Perfect Squares (Backward Direction, Proved)
content: The proved direction: every perfect square $n^2$ (with $n \geq 2$) has $F(n^2) \leq 2$, witnessed by the sequence $[n^2-1, n^2]$. The key identity is $(n^2-1)! \cdot (n^2)! = ((n^2-1)!)^2 \cdot n^2$, which is a perfect square.

title: Known Results (Axiomatized)
content: Four deep results from Erdős-Graham (1976) axiomatized: (1) `D2_eq_squares`: $D_2$ = perfect squares; (2) `no_square_factorial_product_for_primes`: primes excluded from $D_2$; (3) `Dk_empty_above_6`: $D_k = \emptyset$ for $k \geq 7$; (4) `D6_smallest`: 527 is the smallest element of $D_6$.
mathContext: $D_2 = \{m^2 : m \geq 2\}$, $p$ prime $\Rightarrow p \notin D_2$, $D_k = \emptyset$ for $k \geq 7$, $\min D_6 = 527$.

title: Derived Theorems
content: `bigF_prime_zero` shows $F(p) = 0$ for primes (undefined), and `no_prime_in_Dk` shows primes belong to no $D_k$. Both derived from the axioms by case analysis.
mathContext: $p$ prime $\Rightarrow F(p) = 0$ (undefined) $\Rightarrow p \notin D_k$ for all $k \geq 2$.

title: Growth Rate Question (OPEN)
content: The open question: how does $|D_k|$ grow for $3 \leq k \leq 6$? Erdős and Graham showed each $D_k$ is finite but did not determine the growth rate. The axiom `erdos_374_growth_rate` encodes this as the existence of bounds on $|D_k \cap [1,N]|$.
mathContext: Open: determine $|D_k|$ for $3 \leq k \leq 6$, or the counting function $|D_k \cap [1,N]|$ as $N \to \infty$.
